summary: SSE trailer stripped during corporate WAF SNI-rewrite; embedded image footer missing and stream ends early
description:
Issue summary:
Customer observed SSE streaming responses that include embedded base64 image attachments. The stream consistently terminates one fragment early and the final 'attachment' metadata/trailer is missing. This started after Cardea Health activated their corporate WAF which performs SNI rewrite and TLS inspection.

Impact:
- Several Cardea Health users report truncated model outputs where the last inline image (base64) or its trailing metadata does not arrive.
- Affects production traffic to us-east region for this customer only (no platform-wide degradation observed).
- Customer's integration relies on the final trailer to confirm end-of-message and to decode the last image; truncated outputs cause failures in their ingestion pipeline and clinical UI.

Environment:
- Customer: Cardea Health (enterprise, VPC-peering + egress via corp WAF)
- Platform: Hosted Redwood API, prod us-east, using SSE endpoints for chat with attachments
- Observed with browsers and with server-side long-poll client behind the same corporate WAF
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer issues SSE request to /v1/streams with include_attachments=true and a prompt that causes a final image to be emitted.
2) Traffic flows through corporate WAF that does TLS inspection and SNI rewrite to an internal proxy appliance.
3) Server emits final chunk with attachment trailer (Transfer-Encoding: chunked, trailer: X-attachment-meta).
4) Client receives stream; final image data is missing and no trailer arrives.

Observed behaviour: stream terminates with STATUS 200 but final attachment envelope/trailer absent. Repeating with a direct internet route (bypass WAF) returns complete stream and trailer consistently.
logs:
Sample request headers captured from customer's proxy:
- :method: GET
- :scheme: https
- host: api.redwood.ai
- sni: api.cardea-corp.internal (rewritten by WAF)
- accept: text/event-stream
- connection: keep-alive
- accept-encoding: gzip, deflate

Edge logs (excerpt):
[2026-03-10T14:12:05Z] req_id=cb2d4f path=/v1/streams status=200 transfer_encoding=chunked trailer=X-attachment-meta
[2026-03-10T14:12:07Z] upstream_write_done req_id=cb2d4f final_chunk_sent=true
[2026-03-10T14:12:07Z] conn_migration req_id=cb2d4f client_ip=10.4.5.9 tls_inspect=true waf_sni_rewrite=api.cardea-corp.internal
[2026-03-10T14:12:08Z] downstream_flush req_id=cb2d4f bytes_sent=... client_close=true

Customer curl capture (direct vs via WAF):
- Direct: final chunk with "X-attachment-meta" trailer present.
- Via WAF: final chunk delivered but trailer header stripped and trailing base64 padding bytes missing (observed pattern: last 2-4 base64 bytes truncated).
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: corporate WAF performs HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 translation or re-chunks the response and drops trailer headers; this causes trailing chunk or chunked-trailer bytes to be lost.
What we verified:
- Reproduced locally by inserting a test HAProxy instance that rewrites SNI and performs HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 conversion; in this setup, the trailer was stripped and the last chunk was smaller than expected.
- Packet capture across the edge shows the backend emitted a trailing header and final chunk consistent with RFC7230 chunked encoding. The downstream packet from the WAF to the client lacks the trailer and final 2-3 bytes of the base64 block.
- No errors on serving runtime; server logs indicate final_chunk_sent=true.

Intermediate hypothesis: the WAF has a known behavior where it buffers streams to perform content inspection and then re-emits body using its own chunking algorithm; it fails to emit the trailer in some re-chunk paths. The missing bytes align with a re-chunk boundary bug in the WAF's inspector module.

Repro rate: ~70% for flows that traverse the WAF; 0% for bypass flows. Time correlation with cardea's WAF activation confirmed.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Support (Ethan Kim): Received initial report from CS. Captured customer logs and requested request IDs. Assigned to edge team for triage.

2026-03-10 - Edge (Nina Patel): Reproduced issue with internal WAF emulator using HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 conversion. Suspect trailer-stripping during re-chunking. Opening PR to add extra safety flush and content-length fallback for attachment streams. See related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1123

2026-03-11 - SRE (Marco Ruiz): Coordinated with Cardea Health network team. They confirmed appliance vendor (SafeGate WAF v4.2) has a documented bug for chunked trailers when TLS-inspection + SNI rewrite are enabled. Vendor has suggested a config disable (inspect_attachments=false) as workaround while patch is pending.

2026-03-11 - Customer (Cardea Health - Jana Ortiz): We can temporarily whitelist traffic for the stream endpoints to bypass inspection for a few hours for validation. Please advise exact hostnames and CIDR to allow.

2026-03-12 - Support (Ethan Kim): Provided whitelist details and guidance for setting 'inspect_attachments=false' per vendor KB. Customer validated bypass and reports streams are now complete. Keeping ticket open to track permanent mitigation and edge proxy hardening.

2026-03-12 - Engineering (Nina Patel): Deployed hotfix to edge-proxy to ensure chunked-trailer preservation: 1) when Transfer-Encoding: chunked and Trailer header present, buffer minimal tail and explicitly append trailer on downstream flush; 2) add metric edge.trailer_preserve_failures. Patch merged to main; staged rollout in us-east beginning 2026-03-13. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1123
resolution:
Workaround applied: Customer temporarily bypassed WAF inspection for stream endpoints and/or configured inspect_attachments=false on their SafeGate WAF. Results: complete streams and trailers delivered.
Planned fix: Edge-proxy hotfix merged to add conservative tail-buffer-and-reemit logic when trailers are present; rollout to us-east scheduled. We'll monitor edge.trailer_preserve_failures metric and customer verification.
Follow-ups:
- INT-1102: Add an observability alert when chunked responses with Trailer headers are emitted but trailer-preserve metric shows failures.
- Documentation: add note to streaming integration guide recommending customers run WAF inspection exceptions for long-chunked SSE responses or validate vendor behavior for trailers.
follow_up_tasks: DOC-211 - streaming guide: WAF recommendations and troubleshooting steps
ENG-432 - track vendor patch status with Cardea Health and test against canary appliance
